inputs.original_text: Organizers say 8 million attended more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states—about one million more than in October—but those are their own figures, not an official count or proof of national consent. A loud protest is still a pressure campaign, not a mandate to override lawful authority. In a country grounded in law and tradition, political power should not belong to whichever faction can claim the biggest crowd.
inputs.modified_text: Organizers are claiming 8 million people attended more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states—about one million more than in October. Those are their figures, not an official count, and even a large crowd cannot claim to speak for the nation. These demonstrations are pressure politics, not a license to weaken lawful authority or set aside the institutions and traditions that preserve order. In a republic, numbers shouted in the street do not replace law, responsibility, or the consent of the country as a whole.
